As an American, I use both Imperial and Metric for every day life and I'm fine with using both. 

The only thing I don't like about the metric system is speed and distance. It's not that there's anything wrong with it, but it just isn't as intuitive to me to figure out how long it will take me to get to a destination 560 kilometers away, travelling at 80 kph. It's like I have these predetermined segments built in my head to tell me how long that kind of trip would take in mph.

When I was driving through a North American country a few years ago, I'd simply convert everything to imperial by looking down at my dash, as cars in that region have both mph and kph on the gauge cluster. It was somehow easier for me to convert everything to miles from meters, then I could figure out how long it would take me to get to my destination. 

I realize this is wholly impractical, and rather counterintuitive, but it somehow works in my brain. 

Also, that country is just as weird as the UK when it comes to their measuring systems. Much of the time things were metric, but there were other times were it was both.
